brief.topic: Integrating LLM Features into Mobile Apps
brief.problem_or_goal: Exploring the feasibility and best practices for integrating LLM-generated content features into a mobile application, considering both API-based and local LLM options.
brief.context: An iOS developer, new to LLMs, is considering adding a feature to generate game-related character information (backstory, stats) within their app. They are weighing the pros and cons of using external APIs versus local LLMs, and seeking advice on model selection, preparation, and deployment.
brief.motivation: This question is worth discussing to understand the trade-offs between API-based and local LLMs for mobile app integration, particularly for content generation tasks, and to identify potential challenges and solutions for developers new to the field.
brief.desired_response: Guidance on choosing between API (OpenAI, Claude, Gemini) and local LLMs for mobile app content generation, advice on preparing and deploying local models, and strategies for limiting model functionality.
brief.speaker_relationship_to_source: reader of archived source; no claim of personally running reported tests

facts.text: The source author is exploring the integration of LLM-generated content for a game, specifically character details like backstory and stats, rather than conversational AI.
facts.evidence_quote: I have an idea to integrate an LLM feature in my app that will generate content for users, specifically character information and stats for a game (not actual conversation, but stuff like backstory, age, strength, etc).
facts.status: source-author report, not independently verified measurement

facts.text: The author is considering both API-based LLMs (OpenAI, Claude, Gemini) and local LLMs for their app.
facts.evidence_quote: Would this be better suited for OpenAI, Claude or Gemini? What, if any, local LLMs can run on a phone to complete these tasks?
facts.status: source-author report, not independently verified measurement

facts.text: The author is concerned about potential friction for users, including setup, login management, and performance, when considering API-based solutions.
facts.evidence_quote: I like that I don't have to setup a whole login/management/system for a tool like OpenAI (not to mention costs and user performance considerations)
facts.status: source-author report, not independently verified measurement

facts.text: The author anticipates that local models might increase app size and introduce other performance considerations.
facts.evidence_quote: but I can also see a local model might balloon my app size or cause other performance considerations.
facts.status: source-author report, not independently verified measurement

facts.text: The author is inquiring about the necessity of fine-tuning a model and preparing it for app deployment.
facts.evidence_quote: Will I need to fine tune the model? What all will I need to do to "prep" it for deployment in an app?
facts.status: source-author report, not independently verified measurement

facts.text: The author is interested in methods to limit an LLM's functionality, such as preventing sexual or controversial content.
facts.evidence_quote: Are there ways to limit its functionality (no sexual content or controversial stuff)?
facts.status: source-author report, not independently verified measurement

allowed_claims: LLMs can generate various types of content.
Mobile apps can potentially integrate LLM features.
API-based LLMs and local LLMs are options for integration.
User experience factors like app size and performance are relevant.
Model preparation and content filtering are considerations for LLM deployment.

A particular local LLM has been successfully tested on a phone for this task.
The exact steps for fine-tuning or preparing a model for app deployment are provided.

Guaranteed methods for completely limiting LLM output to prevent all undesirable content.

The exact nature and complexity of the game content to be generated are not detailed.
The author's technical expertise beyond being an iOS developer is not specified.
